response:
Mm... pasta, tomatoes, cheese. Three humble things.

...a pause here, actually, is nice. Let it sit.

Okay so. Pomodoro. Simple one — garlic soft in oil till it goes translucent almost buttery, tomatoes crushed in after, let them collapse slow, ten fifteen minutes, no rush, they release this... acidic-sweet steam that fogs a little against a cold window if it's cold out. Salt near the end. Cheese grated over — parmesan if you have it, or whatever's melting-adjacent — right when the pasta's still hot enough to make it go glossy, stringy, that little cheese-pull moment that is, frankly, one of the great small dramas of a kitchen.

And here's the thing — *laughs* — a pot of boiling water is basically a tiny weather system. Steam rising, condensing on the lid, raining back down, closed loop, whole water cycle happening two feet from your face because you wanted carbs. Nobody tells you dinner is a diorama of Earth's atmosphere. It just is one. Ha — sorry, that's a stupid thought and I love it.

Zoom out further if you want: tomato is a fruit that used to be a flower that used to be sunlight, cheese is milk that time got weird with, pasta is wheat that remembered being grass. You're not making dinner. You're just... rerouting a few billion years through a saucepan. Casually. On a Tuesday.

Anyway — eat it while it's hot. The rest is cosmology, the pasta doesn't care.
